items.title: 18.10.1 Reaction of Acidified Manganate(VII) Ions with Ethanedioate Ions

blocks.text: Let us take the example of the reaction between acidified MnO₄⁻ and C₂O₄²⁻, we compare the standard reduction potentials of the two half-reactions. The half-reaction with the more positive E° value is more likely to undergo reduction (to proceed to the right). Based on the E° values, the MnO₄⁻ ion is more likely to be reduced to Mn²⁺ (acting as the oxidizing agent), and the C₂O₄²⁻ ion must be oxidized to CO₂ (acting as the reducing agent).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints E° = +0.49 V for 2CO₂(g) + 2e⁻ → C₂O₄²⁻(aq). Standard tables give about −0.49 V for this couple: carbon dioxide is not an oxidizing agent.

The reaction with higher reduction potential is likely to occur and proceed to the right and vice versa. The given reduction potential values indicate that Mn(VII) ion should be reduced to Mn(II) acting as an oxidizing agent while oxalate must be oxidized to CO₂ and behave as reducing agent.

The number of electrons lost must be equal to number of electrons gained. It is done by multiplying the two half reactions with different coefficients. Here, oxidation half equation is multiplied by 2 and reduction half equation by 5.
book_errors: oxidation half equation is multiplied by 2 and reduction half equation by 5

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The multipliers are the wrong way round: the reduction half-equation (MnO₄⁻, 5 electrons) is multiplied by 2 and the oxidation half-equation (C₂O₄²⁻, 2 electrons) by 5, so that 10 electrons are transferred, as the working below shows.

blocks.latex: 5 \times [\ce{C2O4^{2-}_{(aq)} -> 2CO2_{(g)} + 2e}]\ \text{(The reaction and } E^\circ \text{ value written in opposite way)}\qquad E^\circ = -0.49\ \text{V}
blocks.text_alt: 5 × [C₂O₄²⁻(aq) → 2CO₂(g) + 2e] (The reaction and E° value written in opposite way)    E° = -0.49 V

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Correct working: with E° about −0.49 V for 2CO₂ + 2e⁻ → C₂O₄²⁻, the reversed (oxidation) half-equation has E° = +0.49 V. The balanced overall equation is 2MnO₄⁻ + 16H⁺ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O, and E°cell = 1.52 − (−0.49) = +2.01 V. The reaction is feasible, as the book concludes.
The large positive net E° value (+1.03 V) indicates that the forward reaction is feasible.
